name: Orbicularis oculi
description: Circular muscle surrounding the eye.
clue: Look for the ring around the eyelids.
action: Closes the eyelids.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Orbicularis oris
description: Circular muscle surrounding the mouth.
clue: The muscle encircles the lips.
action: Closes and purses the lips.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Masseter
description: Thick muscle on the lateral jaw.
clue: Find it over the mandibular ramus, just in front of the ear.
action: Elevates the mandible to close the jaw.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Sternocleidomastoid
description: Oblique strap along the side of the neck.
clue: Runs from the sternum/clavicle toward the mastoid region behind the ear.
action: Together: flex the neck. One side: tilts the head to the same side and rotates the face to the opposite side.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Trapezius
description: Broad superficial muscle of the posterior neck and upper back.
clue: Together the two sides form a large diamond.
action: Extends the head/neck; elevates, retracts, depresses and upwardly rotates the scapula through different fiber regions.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Rectus abdominis
description: Paired vertical muscles on the anterior abdomen.
clue: The segmented “six-pack” on either side of the midline.
action: Flexes the trunk and compresses the abdomen.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: External oblique
description: Superficial lateral abdominal muscle.
clue: Fibers run downward and toward the midline.
action: Flexes and laterally bends the trunk; rotates it to the opposite side; compresses the abdomen.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Internal oblique
description: Abdominal muscle deep to the external oblique.
clue: Its upper fibers generally run upward and toward the midline.
action: Flexes and laterally bends the trunk; rotates it to the same side; compresses the abdomen.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Erector spinae group
description: Long columns of muscle along the posterior vertebral column.
clue: Includes iliocostalis, longissimus and spinalis; study them as this listed group.
action: Extends and laterally bends the vertebral column; helps maintain upright posture.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Deltoid
description: Triangular muscle forming the shoulder cap.
clue: Covers the lateral shoulder.
action: Abducts the arm. Anterior fibers assist flexion and posterior fibers assist extension.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Pectoralis major
description: Large fan-shaped muscle on the anterior chest.
clue: Broad on the chest and narrows toward the upper arm.
action: Flexes, adducts and medially rotates the arm.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Latissimus dorsi
description: Broad superficial muscle over the lower posterior trunk.
clue: Sweeps from the lower back toward the upper arm.
action: Extends, adducts and medially rotates the arm.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Biceps brachii
description: Superficial two-headed muscle on the anterior upper arm.
clue: Anterior to the humerus and superficial to brachialis.
action: Flexes the forearm at the elbow and supinates the forearm.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Triceps brachii
description: Three-headed muscle on the posterior upper arm.
clue: Look on the back of the arm, opposite biceps.
action: Extends the forearm at the elbow.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Brachialis
description: Elbow flexor deep to biceps on the anterior humerus.
clue: Visible beside and beneath the distal biceps; use deep view.
action: Flexes the forearm at the elbow.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Brachioradialis
description: Superficial muscle along the lateral, thumb-side forearm.
clue: Crosses the lateral elbow and runs toward the distal radius.
action: Flexes the forearm at the elbow, especially with the thumb pointing upward.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Iliopsoas
description: Deep hip-flexor group formed by iliacus and psoas major.
clue: Seen inside the pelvis and beside the lumbar spine; use deep view.
action: Flexes the thigh at the hip.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Gluteus maximus
description: Large superficial buttock muscle.
clue: Forms most of the posterior buttock contour.
action: Extends and laterally rotates the thigh.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Gluteus medius
description: Fan-shaped muscle on the lateral hip, partly deep to gluteus maximus.
clue: Find it above and lateral to gluteus maximus.
action: Abducts the thigh and helps stabilize the pelvis during walking.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Sartorius
description: Long superficial strap crossing the anterior thigh diagonally.
clue: Runs from the lateral hip to the medial knee.
action: Flexes, abducts and laterally rotates the thigh; flexes the knee.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Quadriceps femoris group
description: Anterior thigh group: rectus femoris and the three vastus muscles.
clue: Includes the central rectus femoris, lateral/medial masses and deeper vastus intermedius.
action: Extends the leg at the knee. Rectus femoris also flexes the thigh at the hip.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Biceps femoris
description: Lateral hamstring on the posterior thigh.
clue: Its distal tendon runs toward the lateral knee.
action: Flexes the knee; its long head also extends the thigh.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Semitendinosus
description: Superficial medial hamstring.
clue: Recognize the long, narrow distal tendon.
action: Extends the thigh and flexes the knee.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Semimembranosus
description: Broad medial hamstring deep to semitendinosus.
clue: Has a broad, flattened proximal tendon; use deep view.
action: Extends the thigh and flexes the knee.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Gastrocnemius
description: Two-headed superficial calf muscle.
clue: Forms the prominent upper posterior calf.
action: Plantarflexes the foot and assists knee flexion.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Tibialis anterior
description: Muscle along the front-lateral side of the tibia.
clue: Anterior shin muscle whose tendon crosses the front of the ankle.
action: Dorsiflexes and inverts the foot.
objective: Unit 10: identify listed muscles and describe their actions

name: Origin
description: The usually more stationary attachment of a muscle; often the proximal attachment.
clue: Distinguish the attachment that usually remains relatively fixed.
objective: Unit 10 vocabulary: origin

name: Insertion
description: The usually more movable attachment of a muscle; often the distal attachment.
clue: During many contractions it moves toward the origin.
objective: Unit 10 vocabulary: insertion

name: Epimysium
description: Connective tissue sheath surrounding the entire muscle.
clue: Epi = outside the whole muscle.
objective: Unit 11: identify skeletal muscle microanatomy / neuromuscular junction structures

name: Perimysium
description: Connective tissue surrounding a fascicle, or bundle of muscle fibers.
clue: Look around one bundle inside the muscle.
objective: Unit 11: identify skeletal muscle microanatomy / neuromuscular junction structures

name: Endomysium
description: Fine connective tissue around an individual muscle fiber.
clue: Look between individual fibers inside a fascicle.
objective: Unit 11: identify skeletal muscle microanatomy / neuromuscular junction structures

name: Fascicle (muscle)
description: A bundle of skeletal muscle fibers.
clue: A bundle inside the whole muscle; its covering is perimysium.
objective: Unit 11: identify skeletal muscle microanatomy / neuromuscular junction structures

name: Skeletal muscle fiber
description: One long skeletal muscle cell containing many myofibrils.
clue: A fiber is a cell; a fascicle contains many fibers.
objective: Unit 11: identify skeletal muscle microanatomy / neuromuscular junction structures

name: Sarcolemma
description: The plasma membrane surrounding a muscle fiber.
clue: The cell membrane, not a connective tissue sheath.
objective: Unit 11: identify skeletal muscle microanatomy / neuromuscular junction structures

name: Myofibrils
description: Long contractile organelles within a muscle fiber, made of repeating sarcomeres.
clue: Many parallel rods fit inside one muscle fiber.
objective: Unit 11: identify skeletal muscle microanatomy / neuromuscular junction structures

name: Myofilaments
description: Protein filaments within myofibrils; thick filaments contain myosin and thin filaments contain actin.
clue: Smaller than a myofibril.
objective: Unit 11: identify skeletal muscle microanatomy / neuromuscular junction structures

name: Sarcoplasmic reticulum
description: Membrane network surrounding myofibrils that stores calcium ions.
clue: Weblike network wrapped around the myofibrils.
objective: Unit 11: identify skeletal muscle microanatomy / neuromuscular junction structures

name: T-tubules
description: Inward extensions of the sarcolemma into the muscle fiber.
clue: A transverse tube runs into the cell.
objective: Unit 11: identify skeletal muscle microanatomy / neuromuscular junction structures

name: Motor end plate
description: Specialized folded region of muscle sarcolemma facing a motor neuron terminal.
clue: The muscle side of the neuromuscular junction.
objective: Unit 11: identify skeletal muscle microanatomy / neuromuscular junction structures

name: Myelin sheath
description: Insulating wrapping around a motor neuron axon approaching a muscle.
clue: Wraps the axon; the terminal itself is unmyelinated.
objective: Unit 11: identify skeletal muscle microanatomy / neuromuscular junction structures

name: Skeletal muscle tissue
description: Long, parallel, striated fibers with multiple peripheral nuclei.
clue: Look for striations and nuclei at the fiber edges.
objective: Unit 11: distinguish skeletal, cardiac and smooth muscle

name: Cardiac muscle tissue
description: Striated, branching cells with central nuclei and intercalated discs.
clue: Branches and intercalated discs distinguish it from skeletal muscle.
objective: Unit 11: distinguish skeletal, cardiac and smooth muscle

name: Smooth muscle tissue
description: Spindle-shaped cells with a central nucleus and no striations.
clue: Look for tapered cells and absence of banding.
objective: Unit 11: distinguish skeletal, cardiac and smooth muscle

name: Sarcomere
description: Repeating unit within a myofibril, extending from one Z disc to the next.
clue: Boundaries are the two Z discs.
objective: Unit 11: identify skeletal muscle microanatomy / neuromuscular junction structures

name: A band
description: Region spanning the full length of thick filaments.
clue: The central dark band.
objective: Unit 11: identify skeletal muscle microanatomy / neuromuscular junction structures

name: I band
description: Region containing thin filaments without thick filaments.
clue: The lighter band on either side of a Z disc.
objective: Unit 11: identify skeletal muscle microanatomy / neuromuscular junction structures

name: Z disc
description: Boundary of a sarcomere where thin filaments are anchored.
clue: A boundary line, not the middle line.
objective: Unit 11: identify skeletal muscle microanatomy / neuromuscular junction structures

name: H zone
description: Central region of the A band containing thick filaments without thin filaments.
clue: Central thick-only zone.
objective: Unit 11: identify skeletal muscle microanatomy / neuromuscular junction structures

name: M line
description: Proteins supporting thick filaments at the center of a sarcomere.
clue: The midline.
objective: Unit 11: identify skeletal muscle microanatomy / neuromuscular junction structures

name: Axon terminal (NMJ)
description: Swollen ending of a motor neuron that faces a muscle fiber.
clue: The neuron side of the neuromuscular junction.
objective: Unit 11: identify skeletal muscle microanatomy / neuromuscular junction structures

name: Synaptic vesicles (NMJ)
description: Small sacs inside a motor neuron terminal that contain acetylcholine.
clue: Small spheres inside the terminal.
objective: Unit 11: identify skeletal muscle microanatomy / neuromuscular junction structures

name: Synaptic cleft (NMJ)
description: Narrow space between the neuron terminal and motor end plate.
clue: The gap between the two cells.
objective: Unit 11: identify skeletal muscle microanatomy / neuromuscular junction structures

name: Cell body
description: The part of a neuron containing its nucleus and most organelles.
clue: The enlarged central portion.
objective: Unit 12: identify neuron structures and describe nervous tissue / synapse microanatomy

name: Dendrite
description: Branching process extending from the cell body, typically receiving input.
clue: Short, branching extensions near the cell body.
objective: Unit 12: identify neuron structures and describe nervous tissue / synapse microanatomy

name: Axon hillock
description: Tapered region where the axon joins the cell body.
clue: The cone-shaped transition into the axon.
objective: Unit 12: identify neuron structures and describe nervous tissue / synapse microanatomy

name: Axon
description: Long neuron process that carries signals toward axon terminals.
clue: One main long process leaves the cell body.
objective: Unit 12: identify neuron structures and describe nervous tissue / synapse microanatomy

name: Myelin sheath
description: Insulating wrapping around portions of an axon.
clue: Separate segments wrapped around the axon.
objective: Unit 12: identify neuron structures and describe nervous tissue / synapse microanatomy

name: Node of Ranvier
description: Gap between adjacent segments of myelin.
clue: Find an exposed gap, not a myelinated segment.
objective: Unit 12: identify neuron structures and describe nervous tissue / synapse microanatomy

name: Axon terminal
description: End branch of an axon that communicates with another cell.
clue: Small ending at the far end of the axon.
objective: Unit 12: identify neuron structures and describe nervous tissue / synapse microanatomy

name: Synapse
description: Junction where a neuron communicates with another cell.
clue: Includes the sending ending, gap and receiving region.
objective: Unit 12: identify neuron structures and describe nervous tissue / synapse microanatomy

name: Synaptic vesicle
description: Membrane-bound sac containing neurotransmitter in a terminal.
clue: Small sphere inside the presynaptic ending.
objective: Unit 12: identify neuron structures and describe nervous tissue / synapse microanatomy

name: Synaptic cleft
description: Narrow extracellular gap between the sending and receiving cells.
clue: Space between the membranes.
objective: Unit 12: identify neuron structures and describe nervous tissue / synapse microanatomy

name: Presynaptic neuron
description: The neuron on the sending side of a synapse.
clue: Its terminal contains synaptic vesicles.
objective: Unit 12: identify neuron structures and describe nervous tissue / synapse microanatomy

name: Postsynaptic cell
description: The receiving cell at a synapse.
clue: The receiving membrane lies across the cleft.
objective: Unit 12: identify neuron structures and describe nervous tissue / synapse microanatomy

name: Cerebrum
description: The large cerebral hemispheres forming the upper part of the brain.
clue: The large folded mass above the brainstem.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Frontal lobe
description: Anterior lobe of the cerebrum.
clue: Toward the forehead.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Parietal lobe
description: Superior-posterior part of each cerebral hemisphere, behind the frontal lobe.
clue: On the upper surface behind the frontal lobe.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Temporal lobe
description: Inferolateral cerebral lobe.
clue: On the side of the brain near the temple.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Occipital lobe
description: Posterior cerebral lobe.
clue: At the back of the cerebral hemisphere.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Cerebral cortex
description: Outer layer of gray matter covering the cerebrum.
clue: Follow the outer folded surface.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Corpus callosum
description: Large C-shaped white matter band between the cerebral hemispheres.
clue: The pale arch in a midsagittal section.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Thalamus
description: Paired central masses of the diencephalon.
clue: The oval region below the corpus callosum and above the hypothalamus.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Hypothalamus
description: Region of the diencephalon inferior to the thalamus.
clue: Below and anterior to the thalamus.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Epithalamus
description: Posterior-superior region of the diencephalon, including the pineal gland.
clue: Look posterior to the thalamus; the pineal gland is a landmark within this region.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Midbrain
description: Upper part of the brainstem, between the diencephalon and pons.
clue: Above the pons.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Pons
description: Rounded bulge on the anterior brainstem.
clue: Between the midbrain and medulla.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Medulla oblongata
description: Inferior part of the brainstem, continuous with the spinal cord.
clue: Below the pons and above the spinal cord.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Cerebellum
description: Highly folded structure posterior to the brainstem.
clue: Behind the pons and medulla; smaller folds than the cerebrum.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Ventricles
description: Connected spaces within the brain that contain cerebrospinal fluid.
clue: The lateral, third and fourth ventricles are parts of this cavity system.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Meninges
description: The three protective membranes around the brain and spinal cord.
clue: From outer to inner: dura, arachnoid, pia.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Dura mater
description: Tough outermost meningeal membrane.
clue: The outer membrane.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Arachnoid mater
description: Middle meningeal membrane.
clue: Between dura and pia; spans over surface grooves.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Pia mater
description: Thin innermost meningeal membrane closely attached to nervous tissue.
clue: Follows the tissue surface and its contours.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Spinal cord
description: CNS structure continuous with the medulla and located in the vertebral canal.
clue: In cross-section, gray matter forms a central butterfly shape.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Central canal
description: Small CSF-containing canal at the center of the spinal cord.
clue: Tiny opening at the center of the gray matter.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Dorsal root ganglion
description: Swelling on the dorsal root containing sensory neuron cell bodies.
clue: A swollen region outside the spinal cord on the dorsal root.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Dorsal root
description: Root through which sensory fibers enter the spinal cord.
clue: Connected with the dorsal root ganglion.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Ventral root
description: Root through which motor fibers leave the spinal cord.
clue: The root without a dorsal root ganglion.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Dorsal horn
description: Posterior projection of spinal gray matter.
clue: The narrower, pointed posterior horn.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Ventral horn
description: Anterior projection of spinal gray matter.
clue: The broader, rounded anterior horn.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Lateral horn
description: Lateral projection of spinal gray matter, prominent in thoracic and upper lumbar levels.
clue: Small side projection between dorsal and ventral horns.
objective: Unit 13: identify listed brain / spinal cord structures on models and specimens

name: Epineurium
description: Connective tissue surrounding an entire peripheral nerve.
clue: The outer covering of the whole nerve.
objective: Unit 14: listed peripheral nerve / reflex-arc vocabulary

name: Perineurium
description: Connective tissue surrounding a nerve fascicle.
clue: A covering around one bundle of nerve fibers.
objective: Unit 14: listed peripheral nerve / reflex-arc vocabulary

name: Endoneurium
description: Fine connective tissue around an individual nerve fiber.
clue: The smallest connective tissue covering inside a fascicle.
objective: Unit 14: listed peripheral nerve / reflex-arc vocabulary

name: Fascicle (nerve)
description: A bundle of nerve fibers within a peripheral nerve.
clue: One bundle within the whole nerve.
objective: Unit 14: listed peripheral nerve / reflex-arc vocabulary

name: Cranial nerves
description: Nerves associated with the brain or brainstem.
clue: There are 12 numbered pairs.
objective: Unit 14: listed peripheral nerve / reflex-arc vocabulary

name: Spinal nerves
description: Nerves connected with the spinal cord; formed where dorsal and ventral roots join.
clue: Contain both sensory and motor fibers.
objective: Unit 14: listed peripheral nerve / reflex-arc vocabulary

name: Sensory neuron
description: Carries sensory information toward the CNS.
clue: Afferent = arriving at the CNS.
objective: Unit 14: listed peripheral nerve / reflex-arc vocabulary

name: Interneuron
description: Neuron within the CNS that connects and processes information between neurons.
clue: An integrating neuron; not every reflex requires an interneuron in its main pathway.
objective: Unit 14: listed peripheral nerve / reflex-arc vocabulary

name: Motor neuron
description: Carries output from the CNS to an effector.
clue: Efferent = exiting the CNS.
objective: Unit 14: listed peripheral nerve / reflex-arc vocabulary

name: Olfactory nerve (CN I)
description: Cranial nerve I.
clue: Small fibers on the inferior frontal region.
action: Smell.
objective: Unit 14: identify and describe the functions of all 12 cranial nerves

name: Optic nerve (CN II)
description: Cranial nerve II.
clue: Runs toward the optic chiasm.
action: Vision.
objective: Unit 14: identify and describe the functions of all 12 cranial nerves

name: Oculomotor nerve (CN III)
description: Cranial nerve III.
clue: Emerges from the ventral midbrain.
action: Most eye movements; raises the upper eyelid; constricts the pupil and adjusts the lens for near vision.
objective: Unit 14: identify and describe the functions of all 12 cranial nerves

name: Trochlear nerve (CN IV)
description: Cranial nerve IV.
clue: Slender nerve that emerges dorsally and wraps around the midbrain.
action: Controls the superior oblique muscle of the eye.
objective: Unit 14: identify and describe the functions of all 12 cranial nerves

name: Trigeminal nerve (CN V)
description: Cranial nerve V.
clue: Large nerve attached to the side of the pons.
action: Facial sensation and muscles of chewing.
objective: Unit 14: identify and describe the functions of all 12 cranial nerves

name: Abducens nerve (CN VI)
description: Cranial nerve VI.
clue: Near the midline at the pons–medulla junction.
action: Abducts the eye through the lateral rectus muscle.
objective: Unit 14: identify and describe the functions of all 12 cranial nerves

name: Facial nerve (CN VII)
description: Cranial nerve VII.
clue: At the lateral pons–medulla junction, beside VIII.
action: Facial expression; taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue; tear and salivary secretion.
objective: Unit 14: identify and describe the functions of all 12 cranial nerves

name: Vestibulocochlear nerve (CN VIII)
description: Cranial nerve VIII.
clue: Lateral to VII at the pons–medulla junction.
action: Hearing and balance.
objective: Unit 14: identify and describe the functions of all 12 cranial nerves

name: Glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX)
description: Cranial nerve IX.
clue: Upper rootlets on the lateral medulla.
action: Taste and sensation from the posterior one-third of the tongue; assists swallowing and salivation.
objective: Unit 14: identify and describe the functions of all 12 cranial nerves

name: Vagus nerve (CN X)
description: Cranial nerve X.
clue: Rootlets on the lateral medulla below IX.
action: Swallowing and voice; parasympathetic regulation of many thoracic and abdominal organs.
objective: Unit 14: identify and describe the functions of all 12 cranial nerves

name: Accessory nerve (CN XI)
description: Cranial nerve XI.
clue: Long series of rootlets extending toward the upper spinal cord.
action: Moves the head and shoulders through sternocleidomastoid and trapezius.
objective: Unit 14: identify and describe the functions of all 12 cranial nerves

name: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII)
description: Cranial nerve XII.
clue: Rootlets on the anterior medulla, medial to IX–XI.
action: Tongue movement.
objective: Unit 14: identify and describe the functions of all 12 cranial nerves

name: Spinal reflex arc
description: Receptor → sensory neuron → CNS integration → motor neuron → effector.
clue: A simple stretch reflex can have a direct sensory-to-motor synapse; other reflexes involve interneurons.
action: Receptor detects a stimulus; sensory neuron carries input to the CNS; CNS integrates; motor neuron carries output; effector responds.
objective: Unit 14: describe a simple spinal reflex arc

name: Heart
description: Autonomic nervous system effects.
clue: Compare the effect on the same target organ.
action: Sympathetic: increases heart rate and force. Parasympathetic: decreases heart rate.
source: Unit 14 in-lab · pp. 30–31; Unit 14 pre-lab · Table 14.2
objective: Unit 14: describe the effects of both autonomic branches

name: Pupils
description: Autonomic nervous system effects.
clue: Compare the effect on the same target organ.
action: Sympathetic: dilates pupils. Parasympathetic: constricts pupils.
source: Unit 14 in-lab · pp. 30–31; Unit 14 pre-lab · Table 14.2
objective: Unit 14: describe the effects of both autonomic branches

name: Airways
description: Autonomic nervous system effects.
clue: Compare the effect on the same target organ.
action: Sympathetic: dilates bronchioles. Parasympathetic: constricts bronchioles.
source: Unit 14 in-lab · pp. 30–31; Unit 14 pre-lab · Table 14.2
objective: Unit 14: describe the effects of both autonomic branches

name: Digestion
description: Autonomic nervous system effects.
clue: Compare the effect on the same target organ.
action: Sympathetic: generally reduces digestive activity and secretions. Parasympathetic: increases digestive activity and secretions.
source: Unit 14 in-lab · pp. 30–31; Unit 14 pre-lab · Table 14.2
objective: Unit 14: describe the effects of both autonomic branches

name: Energy storage and release
description: Autonomic nervous system effects.
clue: Compare the effect on the same target organ.
action: Sympathetic: mobilizes glucose and fats. Parasympathetic: favors energy storage during rest and digestion.
source: Unit 14 in-lab · pp. 30–31; Unit 14 pre-lab · Table 14.2
objective: Unit 14: describe the effects of both autonomic branches

name: Blood vessels
description: Autonomic nervous system effects.
clue: Compare the effect on the same target organ.
action: Sympathetic activity constricts many skin and abdominal vessels and helps redistribute blood during activity. Most vessels do not have a direct opposing parasympathetic supply.
source: Unit 14 in-lab · pp. 30–31; Unit 14 pre-lab · Table 14.2
objective: Unit 14: describe the effects of both autonomic branches

name: Urinary function
description: Autonomic nervous system effects.
clue: Compare the effect on the same target organ.
action: Sympathetic activity generally favors urine retention. Parasympathetic activity supports bladder emptying.
source: Unit 14 in-lab · pp. 30–31; Unit 14 pre-lab · Table 14.2
objective: Unit 14: describe the effects of both autonomic branches

name: Lens for near vision
description: Autonomic nervous system effects.
clue: Compare the effect on the same target organ.
action: Parasympathetic activity adjusts the lens for near vision.
source: Unit 14 in-lab · pp. 30–31; Unit 14 pre-lab · Table 14.2
objective: Unit 14: describe the effects of both autonomic branches

name: Sympathetic division
description: Autonomic nervous system effects.
clue: Compare the effect on the same target organ.
action: Supports activity and fight-or-flight responses: faster heart rate, larger pupils and airways, and reduced digestion.
source: Unit 14 in-lab · pp. 30–31; Unit 14 pre-lab · Table 14.2
objective: Unit 14: describe the effects of both autonomic branches

name: Parasympathetic division
description: Autonomic nervous system effects.
clue: Compare the effect on the same target organ.
action: Supports rest-and-digest responses: slower heart rate, smaller pupils, and increased digestion.
source: Unit 14 in-lab · pp. 30–31; Unit 14 pre-lab · Table 14.2
objective: Unit 14: describe the effects of both autonomic branches
